html:
The Angolan War of Independence was fought from 1961 to 1974 by three nationalist movements against Portuguese rule, the first of Portugal's colonial wars in Africa.

In January 1961 cotton farmers in Baixa de Cassanje revolted, on 4 February militants attacked prisons in Luanda, and in March the UPA, later the FNLA, launched a rising in the north in which many settlers and Africans were killed. Portugal sent tens of thousands of troops. The MPLA, the FNLA and later UNITA fought Portugal and each other.

The war ended after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon in 1974. The Alvor agreement of January 1975 planned a shared government, but it collapsed, and Angola became independent on 11 November 1975 under Agostinho Neto as the civil war began. Most of the settlers fled to Portugal.
sum: The Angolan War of Independence was fought from 1961 to 1974 by three nationalist movements against Portuguese rule, the first of Portugal's colonial wars in Africa.
